newsitem.title: USA: FAA solicits evidence on forged loading documents.
newsitem.headline: FAA solicits evidence on forged loading documents.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration wants to hear from aviation industry workers who know of deliberate forging of loading documents, an FAA official said Friday.
"If people have information they need to come forward so we can investigate it," FAA spokeswoman Kathleen Bergen said.

The agency made the request after the Miami Herald published accounts Thursday by Fine Air and Aeromar Airlines workers who said they had filed misleading documents about how much weight airplanes were carrying.
The workers said they feared losing their jobs if they did not file the documents.

A Fine Air DC-8 loaded by Aeromar personnel crashed shortly after takeoff from Miami International Airport Aug 7, plunging into a busy commercial district and killing five people, four crew and one person on the ground.
Investigators have focused on the possibility that the plane's cargo, clothing material being shipped to the Dominican Republic, may not have been properly secured.
After the crash, former employees of Fine Air have told local media they knew of misloading of planes.
"We encourage them to come forward. We must have facts and information to base our investigation on," Bergen said. Falsification of loading documents is a crime.
The FAA has a toll free hotline, 1-800-255-1111, to which workers can make anonymous reports.end - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
